target_customer: Operators of wastewater plants, farms and landfills with stranded biogas, and buyers of DME and methanol
problem: About 60% of US biogas is wasted in low margin uses or flared while chemical supply chains stay centralized and fossil dependent.
business_model: Modular container-sized units that convert biogas on site into DME and methanol, sold or operated per site; commercial terms not public
product_category: Hard tech, modular biogas to chemicals reforming

founders.name: George Rose
founders.background_notes: 776 Foundation Climate Fellow (Aug 2025) per company site. One profile lists him as CTO; YC lists CEO.

founders.name: Lucas Zubillaga
education: University of Chicago, double BSc in Molecular Engineering and Physics
founders.background_notes: Led design, construction and operation of a bench-scale reforming unit per YC page.

founders.name: Jona van Oord
founders.background_notes: No prior employers listed on YC page.

competitors.name: Emvolon
competitors.what: MIT spinout with modular systems turning biogas into methanol
competitors.traction_then: pilot at a landfill with Montauk Renewables (date not given)
competitors.funding_then: later raised a $22M Series A; date not stated in snippet

competitors.name: Modular Plant Solutions
competitors.what: Containerized methanol plant design taking biogas or syngas, with a DME add-on

technical_complexity.rationale: Reforming biogas to syngas and then to DME or methanol in a modular unit needs chemical process engineering, IP and real plant operation; the pilot has run 1,800+ hours of syngas per the company.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary process and filed IP plus site and offtake agreements, but process claims are not independently verified and similar modular players exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move found; competitor Emvolon raised a Series A while Rise stayed at pre-seed.

market_need_then: Supply chain shocks and geopolitical events exposed chemical industry fragility; biogas is flared or underused and DME is used as aerosol propellant and propane additive.

branding.domain_note: Uses rise-reforming.com, hyphenated; no acquisition story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven and technical, focused on supply resilience.

branding.community_and_virality: Won the European Aerosols Federation 2025 Start-Up Award per the company site; no fan or merch evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found nothing about the brand itself; only the company site's award claim and launch coverage exist.

outcome_analysis: Rise Reforming is an active early hard tech startup from three University of Chicago molecular engineers. It has a working pilot container, a conditional DME offtake agreement and a pre-seed, and is raising a larger round for the first plant. The main risks are scale up, capital intensity and well funded modular competitors, none of which has resolved yet.
notes: Funding totals conflict: JETRO says over $600k pre-seed from DOE, Chicago Booth, 776 Foundation and angels and a $6M raise in progress ($750k soft-committed); UChicago says over $1.7M; Dealroom $400k; PitchBook $1.06M. Only the $650k March 2026 pre-seed stated on the company site is recorded as a round, with investors unnamed there. Dealroom also notes a DOE EnergyTech University Prize in 2024 (unverified). Name origin not found.
